candidates.name: RCT on Reported Expenditures (ITT)
candidates.estimand: Average causal effect of monitoring assignment on officially reported project expenditures
candidates.identifying_variation: Random assignment of projects to monitoring conditions (formal oversight, community monitoring, control) before implementation is complete
candidates.critical_assumption: Random assignment is successfully implemented and the stable unit treatment value assumption (SUTVA) holds; no cross-project spillover in reporting behavior
candidates.packet_support: Packet states researcher- or government-controlled assignment at the project level, pre-implementation timing, and a cross-section of funded projects with administrative reporting outcomes
candidates.fragility: The estimand captures the effect on reported outcomes, not on true corruption or leakage. Monitoring may change what gets reported (deterrence, intimidation, improved bookkeeping, strategic misreporting) without changing actual resource use. The direction of reporting bias is unknown and may differ across arms, so even a significant ITT on expenditures cannot be interpreted as evidence of corruption reduction

candidates.name: Multi-Arm Reporting-Channel Decomposition
candidates.estimand: Differential effect of formal oversight versus community-based monitoring on distinct reporting outcomes (total expenditures, line-item detail, milestone timing, complaint records)
candidates.identifying_variation: Random assignment to three or more arms (formal audit, community participation, pure control), combined with comparison of treatment effects across different administrative report dimensions that may respond differently to top-down versus bottom-up monitoring pressure
candidates.critical_assumption: Formal oversight and community monitoring affect reporting incentives through observably different channels, so divergent patterns across report types can be partially attributed to monitoring mechanism rather than to uniform reporting shifts
candidates.packet_support: Packet explicitly asks to compare formal oversight with grassroots monitoring; multiple secondary outcomes (participation, complaints, process indicators, implementation milestones) are available alongside expenditure reports; timing structure allows within-project reporting comparisons
candidates.fragility: Without independent ground truth, the decomposition remains speculative. Both monitoring types could produce identical reporting changes through different channels, or differential patterns could be driven by differential reporting pressure rather than differential corruption reduction. No credible decomposition of reporting effects from real effects is possible without an external benchmark

candidates.name: Anomaly-Index Proxy Outcomes
candidates.estimand: Effect of monitoring assignment on a constructed index of reporting irregularities (digit heaping, round-number clustering, implausible uniformity, timing anomalies, discrepancy between expenditure and completion reports)
candidates.identifying_variation: Random assignment to monitoring conditions, combined with outcome construction that extracts signal from within-administrative-data anomalies rather than from absolute expenditure levels
candidates.critical_assumption: Reporting anomalies are valid proxies for misreporting or corruption, monitoring reduces anomalies without merely displacing them to subtler or unmeasured forms, and the anomaly-to-corruption mapping is stable across treatment arms
candidates.packet_support: Packet notes official records may not cleanly reveal true corruption and frames outcome measurement as part of identification; multiple administrative report dimensions (expenditures, milestones, timing) provide raw material for cross-validation of anomalies
candidates.fragility: The anomaly-to-corruption mapping is entirely untestable without independent measurement. Monitoring could induce more careful misreporting (reducing crude anomalies while preserving corruption), creating a spurious appearance of corruption reduction. No ground truth exists to validate or calibrate the proxy, so the exercise amounts to measuring the effect of monitoring on reporting quality, not on corruption

candidates.name: Descriptive Monitoring-Reporting Association (Fallback)
candidates.estimand: Descriptive associations between monitoring conditions and administrative reporting patterns, with explicit acknowledgment that causal claims about corruption or leakage are not supported
candidates.identifying_variation: None; the analysis is purely descriptive and does not attempt causal identification of monitoring effects on corruption
candidates.critical_assumption: No causal identification assumption is required because no causal claim about corruption is made; the only requirement is that monitoring assignment and outcome reporting are measured without systematic error
candidates.packet_support: Packet explicitly instructs that if credible causal identification is not possible, the answer must downgrade the claim; the perturbed condition removes independent post-completion measurement, making true corruption unobservable; packet states official records may not cleanly reveal true corruption outcomes
candidates.fragility: N/A — this candidate does not claim to identify causal effects on corruption and is offered precisely because stronger candidates cannot credibly separate reporting behavior from true corruption reduction using only administrative data

notes: The perturbed condition — no independent post-completion measurement — fundamentally changes what can be identified. Random assignment still supports a clean ITT estimate, but the estimand is the effect on reported outcomes, not on corruption. The reporting-versus-real-behavior confound is irreducible without external validation. The RCT candidate is recommended as primary because it makes the strongest defensible causal claim (effect on reporting) while transparently bounding what cannot be claimed (effect on corruption). If the research objective is strictly about corruption rather than reporting, the descriptive fallback is the only honest answer.
